title: Residential schools in Alberta
description: Explore three Alberta residential schools, where they were located, and the years they operated, with links to records from the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation.
overviewDescription: The list introduces St. Mary's on the Blood (Kainai Nation) reserve, St. Albert (Youville), and Lesser Slave Lake (St. Peter's). Each entry includes the recorded operating years and links to its archival record for further learning.

activity.heading: Three Alberta residential schools
activity.introduction: Residential schools separated Indigenous children from their families and communities. This list shares basic information about three Alberta schools and links to records from the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation.
activity.sourceLink: Read the archive record for {{name}} from the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation

schools.name: St. Mary's Residential School (Blood)
schools.description: The school was located on the Blood (Kainai Nation) reserve southwest of Lethbridge.

schools.name: St. Albert Residential School (Youville)
schools.description: The school was in St. Albert, northwest of Edmonton, within Treaty 6 territory.

schools.name: Lesser Slave Lake Residential School (St. Peter's)
schools.description: The school was in northern Alberta, northwest of Edmonton, and operated under Anglican Church administration.

journal.summary: Notes from learning about three Alberta residential schools, using records from the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation.

entries.title: St. Mary's Residential School (Blood)
entries.summary: The school operated from 1898 to 1988 on the Blood (Kainai Nation) reserve southwest of Lethbridge.

entries.title: St. Albert Residential School (Youville)
entries.summary: The school operated from 1873 to 1948 in St. Albert, northwest of Edmonton, within Treaty 6 territory.

entries.title: Lesser Slave Lake Residential School (St. Peter's)
entries.summary: The school operated from 1895 to 1932 in northern Alberta, northwest of Edmonton, under Anglican Church administration.
